definition: Audacious means boldly daring; willing to take surprising risks.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word audacious. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know audacious should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The intern made the audacious suggestion that the firm scrap its flagship product and rebuild it from scratch - and the partners, to everyone's surprise, agreed.
A daring move takes real nerve; audacious goes further - boldness so surprising it makes onlookers gasp.
Reckless pushes past audacious and loses the admiration: the audacious climber takes a shocking but calculated line, while the reckless one ignores the weather entirely.

Fearless describes what someone feels - no fear at all - whether or not any risk is taken. Audacious describes what someone does: a move so boldly daring it startles onlookers. A fearless firefighter may follow every rule; an audacious one tries the entry nobody has dared.

Bold is the everyday word for confident and brave, covering everything from a bold answer in class to a bold choice of color. Audacious raises the stakes: boldness surprising enough to make onlookers gasp, a risk most people would never take.

Brazen is boldness with the shame removed - acting openly where most people would at least blush - and the word usually disapproves. Audacious keeps the surprise but not the verdict: an audacious plan startles, and may be admired or condemned for it.

An audacious plan can be carefully calculated; it simply refuses to play safe.
